item.title: Bluesky expands Attie AI tool to create lightweight social apps
item.description:
Bluesky expands Attie AI tool to create lightweight social apps

Bluesky’s Attie AI tool, which launched earlier this year as a way to build your own feeds with AI, now lets users create small social apps – from games to polls – and publish them as individual websites.

🔍 Overview

  • Attie was introduced as a feed‑building AI assistant and is being broadened to support “small” social apps such as games, polls, and dashboards that can be shared with others as their own websites.
  • The tool is positioned by Bluesky as a way to do “social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community.”

🧩 How it works

  • Users create an app simply by typing a natural‑language prompt.
  • The AI generates the functional app in a matter of minutes. For example, “A simple poll I made about Pokémon Red and Pokémon Blue took a few minutes to generate.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Supported app types: games, polls, dashboards, quizzes, idle clickers, and more.

  • Examples highlighted on the Attie site:

    Example Description
    Flappy Butterfly Flappy Bird‑style clone
    Drum machine Simple online drum sequencer
    Quiz Interactive quiz app
    Celery Man idle clicker Idle clicker about a celery man

  • Each example lives on a custom attie.site link with attribution for the creator displayed at the bottom of the page.

  • The apps are described as “pretty lightweight novelties, though I liked the drum machine.”

🚀 Availability

  • Attie apps can be shared instantly as standalone web pages on the attie.site domain.
  • The tool is currently live and can be accessed directly through Bluesky’s platform.

💡 Why it matters

  • By allowing anyone to generate functional mini‑apps with a prompt, Attie lowers the barrier to creating community‑specific tools.
  • Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider framed the vision as “social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community,” emphasizing a shift toward user‑driven, AI‑assisted social experiences.

#Bluesky #Attie #AI #NoCode #SocialApps

Source: Bluesky’s AI tool now lets you make games and apps to share on social

item.title: Hands‑On Workshop Helps Professionals Build Personal AI Systems
item.description:
Hands‑On Workshop Helps Professionals Build Personal AI Systems

A new hands‑on workshop lets participants turn a repetitive work task into a personal AI workflow, requiring no technical background.

🔍 Overview

  • Turn one repetitive task from your real work into an AI workflow.
  • Build Your Personal AI System!
  • Most AI courses show you slides about what AI can do.

🛠️ How It Works

  • This is not a lecture.
  • This is a working session in a tiny group (max 4–5 people) where we sit down and build AI systems for your actual work.
  • You bring your daily friction.
  • We build the AI stack together.
  • Over the session, you will map out your workflow, find where AI actually saves time, set up tools like Claude Code and OpenClaw hands‑on, and leave with a working system you can use Monday morning.
  • Then you get a free follow‑up call to check your progress or fix what broke.

👥 Who Should Attend

  • No experience needed.
  • No technical background required.
  • You just need a challenge you want to solve or curiosity to learn latest tech.
  • This is for any job, any background.
  • If you have work that eats your time, you belong here.
  • Bring a problem.
  • Build a system.
  • One‑size‑fits‑all.

📍 Logistics

  • 📍 Location: May change due to capacity.
  • You will be informed in advance.

💬 Why It Matters

  • “I believe the more we let AI take care of the robotic aspects of our lives, the more time we have for the human parts of it.”

👤 Organizer Insight

  • I have founded 20+ businesses.
  • Some worked.
  • Most didn’t.
  • That is the point.
  • I test fast, fail fast, and keep what works.
  • Right now, I am deep in the world of AI, optimizing my stack for every task and would like to share that knowledge while learning.
  • and a few more as a founding partner or consultant.

#AIWorkshop #Productivity #NoCode #Automation

Source: AI Stack Lab

item.title: AI‑Powered Rapid Landing Page Creation Showcased at Startplatz AI Hub Event
item.description:
AI‑Powered Rapid Landing Page Creation Showcased at Startplatz AI Hub Event

An AI‑focused meetup took place in Cologne, bringing together over 100 vibe coders and marketers each month (more than 2,000 since June 2025). Speakers demonstrated how AI can turn a vague brief into a functional landing page in minutes, and shared workflows for building web‑to‑app experiences without traditional development skills.

🔍 Overview

  • When: 18:30 – 21:00 CEST, doors open at 18:30, talks start at 19:00.
  • Where: Im Mediapark 5, 1st Floor, Room Barcelona, 50670 Cologne, Germany.
    • Transit: Media Park S‑Bahn station – 3 minute walk.
    • Parking: Synodome parking house.
  • Streaming: All sessions streamed live with HD audio and screen share. Register to receive a Zoom link. Talks are recorded and posted on pirateskills.com; participants may appear on video.

🗓️ Event Details

  • Community size: 100+ vibe coders and marketers join each month; 2,000+ participants since June 2025.
  • Organisers: Startplatz AI Hub (the epicenter of generative AI and innovation in Cologne) and Pirate Skills (growth‑marketing community offering courses and tools such as the Captain).
  • Format: Short talks followed by demos of AI‑assisted workflows.

🧑‍💼 Speakers & Topics

Time Speaker Talk Title & Focus
19:00 – 19:15 Ben Sufiani “From Web to App: Pirate Skills in Your Pocket” – built a web‑to‑app solution in a weekend without being a developer, using actions that agents and apps share.
— Christina Röse Non‑technical vibe‑coded the landing page for her wedding site bridesmaid.love, part of an agentic wedding planner she is building.
— Farzan Borhanazad Showed how to turn a vague brief into a polished website in a few hours using Codex, Claude, and design tricks like instant color/font swaps.
— Nurgul Aslan (IADM) Presented a risk‑management fix for AI tools: list, classify risk, assign owner, train, document; explained what the EU AI Act requires.

⚙️ Key Takeaways

  • Cost & speed: Avoid €15k MVP projects that take months; create landing pages in 15 minutes.
  • Analytics: Set up tracking yourself without additional services.
  • Automation: Use AI to handle repetitive tasks such as bug fixes, testing, and documentation.
  • Compliance: Follow EU AI Act guidance by cataloguing tools, assessing risk, and maintaining documentation.

🚀 How to Join the Community

  • Startplatz AI Hub: Free AI workshops, events, and community building – online and in Cologne.
  • Pirate Skills: Join the community, take Ben’s courses, or use tools like the Captain for growth marketing.
  • Registration: Sign up to receive the Zoom link and access live streams.

The event captured the practical potential of generative AI for rapid, low‑code web creation and highlighted compliance considerations for practitioners.

#AIEvents #NoCode #GrowthMarketing #EUAIAct

Source: Vibe Coding Cologne - October 7, 2026 | Free AI-Assisted Coding Meetup

item.title: AutoGPT Launches Hosted Platform for AI Agent Workflow Automation
item.description:
AutoGPT Launches Hosted Platform for AI Agent Workflow Automation

AutoGPT has publicly launched its hosted platform, enabling users to build, deploy, and run AI agents that complete entire workflows. The platform is described as a vision for accessible AI for everyone, aiming to provide tools so users can focus on what matters.

🧩 How it works

AutoGPT allows you to describe an outcome in plain English or build step-by-step in a visual builder. The agent can then run on demand, on a schedule, or from a trigger.

⚙️ Key details

The platform includes several core components:

  • AutoPilot: Describe a job in plain English to create a working agent.
  • Agents: View every agent, its run history, cost, and actions needing attention.
  • Marketplace: Start with proven agents, add them to your library, and customize.
  • Build: A visual builder to drag, connect, branch, and inspect blocks for precise control.

Key technical specifications include:

  • 45+ connected platforms and hundreds of AI models.
  • No need for model API keys or infrastructure setup.
  • The platform manages infrastructure, model access, credentials, reliability, and updates.

🚀 Availability

The hosted platform is a publicly available paid service with usage-based agent runs. A free path is available via self-hosting, where you provide the infrastructure.

💡 Why it matters

The project has garnered significant community interest, with over 185,000 GitHub stars. Several industry figures have commented on its potential. Andrej Karpathy, a founding member of OpenAI, noted that “AutoGPTs” represent a next frontier in prompt engineering. Amjad Masad, co-founder & CEO of Replit, stated that “If you have a phone you can run AutoGPT. You don’t even need to learn how to code.” Lior Alexander, CEO of AlphaSignal, suggested that “AutoGPT might be the next big step in AI.”

#AIagents #NoCode #Automation #AItools #PromptEngineering

Source: Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT

item.title: Quickchat AI Enables No-Code Remote MCP Server Connections for AI Agents
item.description:
Quickchat AI Enables No-Code Remote MCP Server Connections for AI Agents

Quickchat AI has introduced a way to connect AI Agents to remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers with no code on its free plan. This allows an AI Agent to reach out to remote servers to retrieve information dynamically during a live conversation, expanding beyond static knowledge bases.

🧩 How it works

MCP is a standard protocol that allows a server to expose tools to an AI. The server publishes each tool’s name, description, and required arguments, allowing any MCP client to list and execute them. When an Agent uses a remote MCP tool, the integration follows a three-step flow:

  • The model selects a tool: The Agent reviews all enabled tools and their descriptions to decide when to call them.
  • Quickchat AI enforces security and rules: Before transmitting data, the platform checks the tool whitelist, attaches necessary connection headers or OAuth tokens, and blocks addresses resolving to internal networks.
  • The server executes the tool: The server runs the requested tool, returns the data, and the Agent integrates this information into its final response.

Every tool call involves two distinct types of data values. Deterministic values, such as the server URL, headers, and tokens, are completed automatically by the integration. Judgment values, such as specific search queries or repository names, are filled in by the AI model itself.

⚙️ Protocol updates

Recent updates have simplified how remote MCP servers operate. The 2026-07-28 revision of the MCP specification made the core protocol stateless, removed session headers from streamable HTTP, and deprecated the older HTTP-plus-SSE transport. Claude shipped support for these changes the same week.

As a result, a remote MCP server operates as a standard HTTPS endpoint. Quickchat AI natively supports streamable HTTP and provides a fallback to legacy SSE transport if a server’s URL path ends in /sse.

🛠️ Step-by-step example

Users can build a support Agent for Hoist (a resumable file-upload API) that handles both internal knowledge and external live lookups. The setup takes about fifteen minutes and requires a free Quickchat AI account.

  • Internal Knowledge: The Agent natively answers questions about Hoist’s plans, file-size limits, storage regions, and webhooks directly from its uploaded knowledge base.
  • External Knowledge: When asked about the behavior of the open-source tus-js-client library, the Agent queries DeepWiki (a public MCP server by Cognition) to search the library’s live source code on GitHub on demand.

Users can select from an integrated catalog of 242 remote MCP servers or delegate the entire setup to an AI assistant over Quickchat AI’s own MCP server.

#QuickchatAI #ModelContextProtocol #AIAgents #NoCode

Source: Connect Your AI Agent to a Remote MCP Server (2026)
